keyVerseText: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word אֲנוּ (ʼănûw) is a contracted form of אֲנַחְנוּ (ʼănachnûw), which means "we" or "ourselves." This root form emphasizes the first-person plural pronoun, often used for emphasis, underscoring the collective identity and responsibility of the speakers. The contraction suggests a more concise, perhaps colloquial form of the same pronoun, highlighting communal participation and shared agency beyond the simple English translation of "we."
usageInScripture: The word אֲנוּ appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, specifically in Jeremiah 42:6, where it is translated as part of the phrase "to whom we." This limited occurrence shows that while אֲנוּ is rare, it functions consistently as a first-person plural pronoun emphasizing the group’s involvement or commitment. Its use in this key verse reveals a solemn corporate declaration of obedience and submission to God's voice, reflecting the collective faith and responsibility of the people.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲנוּ as a first-person plural pronoun with an emphasis on collective identity deepens our grasp of biblical community and covenant relationship. It reminds believers that faith and obedience are not merely individual acts but corporate commitments to God. This word highlights the unity and shared responsibility of God's people in responding to His commands, reinforcing the biblical truth that salvation and obedience are lived out within the community of faith. Recognizing this communal aspect enriches our appreciation of how God calls His people to walk together in covenant faithfulness.
keyVerseReflection: Jeremiah 42:6 states, "Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God." The use of אֲנוּ here emphasizes the collective commitment of the people to obey God's voice. It underscores their unified decision and shared responsibility before God, expressing a solemn vow that includes every member of the community. This collective pronoun enriches the verse by highlighting the seriousness and inclusiveness of their pledge to follow God's guidance.
